root.label: Intubation Indicated
root.description: Failure to maintain/protect airway, respiratory failure, GCS ≤8

content.title: Consider RSI when:
items: Failure to maintain or protect airway
Respiratory failure despite NIV
GCS ≤8 or rapidly declining consciousness
Need for controlled ventilation (status epilepticus, TBI)
Anticipatory (transfer of unstable patient)

node.label: SOAP-ME Preparation
node.description: Suction, Oxygen, Airway, Pharmacology, Monitoring, Equipment

rows: Yankauer + flexible catheter connected and tested
BVM with appropriate mask, 15 L/min O₂, PEEP valve if available
Laryngoscope blade tested, ETT + backup sizes, stylet loaded, LMA ready
Induction + paralytic drawn up, doses verified by 2nd provider
SpO₂, ETCO₂ (gold standard), cardiac monitor, BP cuff
Tube holder + tape, stethoscope, NG/OG tube

content.notes: ETT, blade, LMA, and depth auto-calculated from patient weight/age in the banner.

node.label: Preoxygenate
node.description: 3-5 min 100% FiO₂ via NRB. Avoid PPV if possible.

items: 3-5 minutes with 100% FiO₂ via non-rebreather mask
Avoid positive-pressure ventilation (reduces aspiration risk)
Consider nasal cannula at max flow during attempt for apneic oxygenation
Infant: shoulder roll to achieve sniffing position (large occiput)
Child: folded towel under occiput for sniffing position

content.title: Ketamine is PREFERRED for rural RSI
items: Hemodynamic stability (does not drop BP)
Bronchodilatory (ideal for asthma)
Preserves respiratory drive during apneic period
Analgesic + amnestic
IM route available (3-5 mg/kg) if no IV access
Safe in shock, asthma, seizures, TBI

content.title: Relative cautions (NOT absolute contraindications)
items: Active psychosis (rare in children)
Known or strongly suspected globe injury
Emergence reactions: treat with low-dose midazolam

rows: No hyperkalemia risk. Reversible with sugammadex.
CONTRAINDICATED: burns >48h, crush, neuromuscular disease, hyperkalemia risk

node.label: Laryngoscopy + Intubation
node.description: Direct visualization of cords. Pass ETT. Confirm.

content.title: ALL of the following:
items: ETCO₂ waveform — GOLD STANDARD (must see consistent waveform)
Bilateral breath sounds (auscultate axillae)
Chest rise with ventilation
Absence of epigastric sounds
SpO₂ trending up or stable
Chest radiograph to confirm position

node.label: Post-Intubation Care
node.description: Secure tube, sedation, ventilator, NG tube

items: Secure ETT with commercial holder + tape
Sedation: Midazolam 0.1 mg/kg q1-2h PRN
Analgesia: Fentanyl 1-2 mcg/kg q1h PRN
Set initial ventilator parameters
Place NG/OG tube to decompress stomach
Chest radiograph for ETT position

content.title: Stepwise rescue
items: Step 1: Insert LMA — ventilate through LMA
Step 2: If LMA fails — BVM with two-person technique
Step 3: Reposition, reattempt with different blade/provider
Step 4 (<8 yr): Needle cricothyrotomy with 14-18G angiocatheter
Step 4 (≥8 yr): Surgical cricothyrotomy with 4.0-6.0 cuffed trach/ETT

content.title: Cannot Intubate, Cannot Oxygenate
content.body: If SpO₂ falling despite BVM and LMA: proceed immediately to surgical airway. Do not make repeated intubation attempts. Oxygenation takes priority over intubation.

textbook.title: Rapid Sequence Intubation in the Rural Emergency Department

blocks.text: Rapid sequence intubation (RSI) is the simultaneous administration of an induction agent and a neuromuscular blocking agent to facilitate endotracheal intubation. In the rural ED, RSI is the most common method of emergency airway management and requires systematic preparation, practiced technique, and a clear failed-airway plan.

Ketamine + Rocuronium is the preferred RSI combination for the rural emergency department. Ketamine preserves hemodynamics, provides bronchodilation, and has a wide safety margin. Rocuronium avoids the hyperkalemia risks of succinylcholine.

The SOAP-ME mnemonic ensures systematic preparation. Every item must be verified before medication administration. All doses should be verified by a second provider. Equipment should be tested — check laryngoscope light, suction pressure, and BVM seal before pushing medications.

blocks.title: Critical Safety Rule
blocks.body: NEVER push the paralytic until you have confirmed you can ventilate the patient with BVM. If you cannot bag the patient, do not paralyze them.

blocks.text: Preoxygenation with 100% FiO₂ for 3-5 minutes creates a nitrogen washout that extends the safe apnea time. In children, this window is shorter than in adults due to higher oxygen consumption relative to FRC. Apneic oxygenation via nasal cannula at maximum flow during the intubation attempt can further extend this window.

Confirmation of ETT placement requires ETCO₂ waveform capnography — this is the gold standard and must be documented. Colorimetric CO₂ detectors are acceptable but waveform is preferred. After confirmation, the tube must be secured, sedation/analgesia initiated, and initial ventilator parameters set based on the underlying condition.
